questions.title: Question 1: Pattern Recognition
questions.text: When looking at complex information or situations, you:

options.A: Quickly identify underlying patterns and connections that others might miss
options.B: Focus on the practical implications and what actions need to be taken
options.C: Notice how different people are affected and their emotional responses
options.D: See the big picture and envision future possibilities and outcomes

questions.title: Question 2: Problem-Solving Instinct
questions.text: When faced with a challenging problem, your first instinct is to:

options.A: Break it down into logical components and analyze each systematically
options.B: Look for the most efficient and practical solution that works immediately
options.C: Consider how the solution will impact all people involved
options.D: Think of creative, unconventional approaches that haven't been tried

questions.title: Question 3: Natural Communication Style
questions.text: In conversations, you naturally tend to:

options.A: Ask probing questions and seek to understand the deeper logic
options.B: Focus on concrete details and actionable next steps
options.C: Pay attention to emotions and help others feel heard and understood
options.D: Share big ideas and inspire others with possibilities

questions.title: Question 4: Energy and Motivation
questions.text: You feel most energized and motivated when:

options.A: Solving complex puzzles or figuring out how things work
options.B: Completing tasks efficiently and seeing tangible results
options.C: Helping others succeed and building meaningful relationships
options.D: Exploring new ideas and imagining what could be possible

questions.title: Question 5: Learning New Skills
questions.text: When learning something new, you naturally:

options.A: Want to understand the underlying principles and theory first
options.B: Jump in and learn through hands-on practice and repetition
options.C: Learn best when you can relate it to people and real-life situations
options.D: See connections to other areas and think of innovative applications

questions.title: Question 6: Decision-Making Approach
questions.text: Your natural decision-making process involves:

options.A: Gathering data, analyzing options, and choosing the most logical solution
options.B: Considering practical constraints and choosing what will work best
options.C: Thinking about how decisions will affect people and relationships
options.D: Imagining multiple scenarios and choosing the most innovative path

questions.title: Question 7: Work Environment Preferences
questions.text: You perform best in environments that:

options.A: Allow for deep thinking, analysis, and intellectual challenges
options.B: Have clear goals, efficient processes, and measurable outcomes
options.C: Emphasize collaboration, teamwork, and positive relationships
options.D: Encourage creativity, flexibility, and exploration of new ideas

questions.title: Question 8: Natural Talents Recognition
questions.text: Others often come to you for:

options.A: Your ability to analyze situations and provide logical insights
options.B: Your practical skills and ability to get things done efficiently
options.C: Your emotional intelligence and ability to understand people
options.D: Your creativity and ability to see new possibilities

questions.title: Question 9: Stress Response
questions.text: Under pressure, you naturally:

options.A: Become more focused and systematic in your approach
options.B: Prioritize tasks and work more efficiently to meet deadlines
options.C: Seek support from others and try to maintain team harmony
options.D: Think outside the box and come up with innovative solutions

questions.title: Question 10: Information Processing
questions.text: You naturally process information by:

options.A: Organizing it logically and looking for cause-and-effect relationships
options.B: Focusing on what's most relevant and immediately useful
options.C: Considering the human element and interpersonal implications
options.D: Making connections to broader concepts and future possibilities

questions.title: Question 11: Leadership Style
questions.text: When in leadership roles, you naturally:

options.A: Lead through expertise and logical decision-making
options.B: Lead by example and focus on achieving concrete results
options.C: Lead by building consensus and supporting team members
options.D: Lead by inspiring others with vision and innovative thinking

questions.title: Question 12: Attention to Detail
questions.text: Your relationship with details is:

options.A: You naturally notice inconsistencies and analytical details
options.B: You focus on details that are practically important for success
options.C: You pay attention to details that affect people's feelings and needs
options.D: You see details as part of larger patterns and possibilities

questions.title: Question 13: Time Management
questions.text: Your natural approach to time is:

options.A: You like to think things through thoroughly before acting
options.B: You prefer to work efficiently and complete tasks quickly
options.C: You balance task completion with maintaining relationships
options.D: You often lose track of time when exploring interesting ideas

questions.title: Question 14: Conflict Resolution
questions.text: When conflicts arise, you instinctively:

options.A: Try to understand the logical basis of each person's position
options.B: Focus on finding practical solutions that resolve the issue
options.C: Work to understand everyone's feelings and find common ground
options.D: Look for creative win-win solutions that address underlying issues

questions.title: Question 15: Innovation and Change
questions.text: Your natural response to new ideas or changes is:

options.A: To analyze them carefully and understand their implications
options.B: To evaluate their practical value and implementation challenges
options.C: To consider how they will affect people and relationships
options.D: To get excited about possibilities and think of improvements

questions.title: Question 16: Memory and Recall
questions.text: You most easily remember:

options.A: Logical systems, theories, and analytical frameworks
options.B: Practical procedures, facts, and step-by-step processes
options.C: Personal stories, emotional experiences, and people's names
options.D: Big ideas, creative concepts, and future possibilities

questions.title: Question 17: Natural Strengths
questions.text: In group projects, others typically rely on you for:

options.A: Research, analysis, and logical problem-solving
options.B: Organization, execution, and getting things done
options.C: Team building, communication, and interpersonal support
options.D: Creative ideas, brainstorming, and innovative solutions

questions.title: Question 18: Feedback Preference
questions.text: You naturally give and prefer to receive feedback that is:

options.A: Objective, specific, and based on logical criteria
options.B: Direct, actionable, and focused on practical improvements
options.C: Supportive, encouraging, and considerate of feelings
options.D: Inspiring, future-focused, and emphasizes potential

questions.title: Question 19: Goal Setting
questions.text: Your natural approach to setting goals involves:

options.A: Creating logical, well-researched objectives with clear metrics
options.B: Setting practical, achievable targets with specific deadlines
options.C: Considering how goals align with personal values and relationships
options.D: Envisioning inspiring possibilities and breakthrough outcomes

questions.title: Question 20: Problem Identification
questions.text: You naturally tend to notice:

options.A: Logical inconsistencies and analytical problems that need solving
options.B: Inefficiencies and practical issues that hinder productivity
options.C: Interpersonal tensions and people who need support
options.D: Missed opportunities and untapped potential for innovation

A.name: Analytical & Technical
A.summary: You excel at pattern recognition, logical analysis, and systematic problem-solving. You naturally break down complexity and find structure.

B.name: Practical & Applied
B.summary: You thrive when completing concrete tasks and seeing tangible results. You are motivated by getting things done and real-world impact.

C.name: Communication & Interpersonal
C.summary: You naturally connect with others, ask probing questions, and communicate ideas clearly. You learn and contribute through dialogue.

D.name: Creative & Innovative
D.summary: You are drawn to new ideas, creative solutions, and exploring possibilities. You think in terms of what could be rather than only what is.
